mainTopic: Whether freeing a slave helps or harms him (רבי מאיר vs. the חכמים), and a new משנה on whether a גט, a שטר שחרור, or a money gift is still given after the sender dies.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר argues that freeing a slave is a חוב (a loss) for him. A runaway slave or a rebellious wife of a כהן still eats תרומה, but a freed slave cannot eat it at all. רבא explains how the חכמים answer this, 'מפני שהוא קנינו': the master could always end the slave's תרומה by selling him to a ישראל. The גמרא then asks how רבי מאיר's view covers a ישראל's slave. The answer is that freedom forbids him a שפחה כנענית, and a slave prefers that loose relationship even over being allowed a free woman. A new משנה follows: a גט or a שטר שחרור is not delivered after the sender dies, but a money gift he ordered is still given. רב limits this to coins piled in a corner. The גמרא asks why piling matters for either a healthy giver or a dying one. רב זביד answers that the giver is healthy and the gift works through מעמד שלשתן. רב פפא answers that the giver is a שכיב מרע and the piling shows which coins he meant, not a buried מנה. The הלכה is that we do not worry about a buried מנה, and the amud ends by asking why רב פפא did not explain it like רב זביד. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's argument: runaway slave and rebellious wife still eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר argues that freedom truly hurts a כהן's slave. Even a runaway slave or a rebellious wife still eats תרומה, but a freed slave cannot eat it at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: Look at a כהן's slave who ran away, or a כהן's wife who rebelled against her husband. Don't they still eat תרומה? But this freed slave does not eat it at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא with רבי מאיר's fuller argument to the חכמים, showing that freeing a slave is a loss for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the slave or wife breaks off from the כהן, they keep their status and can eat other כהנים' תרומה. Freedom, though, takes away his right to תרומה completely. So freedom does something to him that even running away does not, and that proves it is a חוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A slave owned by a כהן, who is allowed to eat תרומה
The holy portion of produce given to כהנים

phrases.english: "And what if a slave of a priest who ran away
or the wife of a priest who rebelled against her husband
do they not eat teruma?
But this one does not eat!"
phrases.notes: "This one" is the slave who was freed. Once free, he can't eat anyone's תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי מאיר's argument from the משנה that freedom is a חוב for the slave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Freedom takes away a כהן's slave's right to תרומה in a way that even running away does not, so it counts as a loss for him.

steps.title: רבי מאיר seems to be right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי מאיר's argument sounds convincing. How can the חכמים answer it?
steps.simpleTranslation: He is speaking well to them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי מאיר's argument looks strong, which puts pressure on the חכמים. This sets up the next step, where רבא explains their answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If running away does not stop the slave from eating תרומה but freedom does, freedom looks like a real loss. That would undercut the חכמים, who say freedom is purely a זכות.

keyTerms.meaning: He is saying it well, a convincing point

phrases.english: He is speaking well to them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רבי מאיר's argument and challenges the חכמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The position of the חכמים that freedom is a זכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Freedom takes away תרומה even more than running away does, so it seems to be a real loss.

steps.title: רבא: the master could sell him to a ישראל anytime
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the חכמים answered in the משנה 'because he is his property'. The master can always take away the slave's תרומה by selling him to a ישראל for four זוז, wherever the slave is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what they answered him in the משנה, 'because he is his property.' If the master wants, he can take four זוז from a ישראל and disqualify the slave from תרומה wherever he is.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends the חכמים by explaining what their short answer in the משנה really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loss of תרומה is not something freedom creates, because the master already had the power to take it away at any time, even from a runaway, by selling him. So freeing him does not take away anything the slave could count on keeping. That means freedom is still a זכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Four זוז, a small sum of money

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the חכמים measure a loss. A right that the master can cancel at will is not a real loss when it is taken away.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: הַיְינוּ דְּקָא מַהְדְּרִי לֵיהּ בְּמַתְנִיתִין:
phrases.english: Rava said: This is what they answered him in the Mishnah:
"Because he is his property."

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי בָּעֵי, שָׁקֵיל אַרְבָּעָה זוּזֵי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: For if he wants, he takes four zuz from an Israelite
and disqualifies him wherever he is.
phrases.notes: Once a ישראל owns him, he is no longer a כהן's slave, so he can't eat תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַיְינוּ דְּקָא מַהְדְּרִי לֵיהּ בְּמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2 on behalf of the חכמים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the meaning of the חכמים' words in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Losing תרומה through freedom is a real loss for the slave.
steps.terutzMaskana: The master can always remove the slave's תרומה by selling him, so freedom does not take away a secure right.

steps.title: How does רבי מאיר explain a slave of a ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר's argument about תרומה only works for a כהן's slave. For a ישראל's slave, who never ate תרומה, what is the loss in freeing him?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי מאיר, this works for a כהן's slave. But what can be said about a ישראל's slave?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges רבי מאיר. His reason only covers a כהן's slave, but he seems to treat every slave the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר lets the master take back any שטר שחרור, because freedom is a חוב. A ישראל's slave never ate תרומה, so he loses nothing there. רבי מאיר needs a different loss for that slave.

keyTerms.meaning: A slave owned by a ישראל (not a כהן)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Meir, this works for a priest's slave;
what is there to say about an Israelite's slave?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending the חכמים to questioning how רבי מאיר's reason applies to every slave.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's view that freeing any slave is a חוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תרומה loss does not exist for a ישראל's slave, so where is the חוב?

steps.title: He loses the שפחה כנענית
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק answers that freedom makes a שפחה כנענית forbidden to the slave. That is his loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק said: Because the master makes him lose the שפחה כנענית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי מאיר a different loss that applies to every slave, even a ישראל's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As a slave, he was allowed to be with a שפחה כנענית. Once he is free, she becomes forbidden to him. Losing that permission is the חוב that freedom causes.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish maidservant owned by a Jew

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak said:
Because he makes him lose the Canaanite maidservant.
phrases.notes: While he is a slave, she is permitted to him. Once he is free, she is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּפְסִידוֹ מִשִּׁפְחָה כְּנַעֲנִית
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different loss that applies to all slaves
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ישראל's slave loses nothing when he is freed.
steps.terutzMaskana: He loses the permission to be with a שפחה כנענית.

steps.title: But he gains a free woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that freedom also helps him, because now he may marry a free Jewish woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! The master is permitting him to a free woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 5. Freedom brings a gain that seems to outweigh the loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He loses the שפחה, but he gains the right to marry a בת חורין. That seems like an upgrade, so the loss of the שפחה should not make freedom a חוב.

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַבָּה, הֲרֵי הוּא מַתִּירוֹ בְּבַת חוֹרִין!
phrases.english: On the contrary, he permits him to a free woman!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, הֲרֵי הוּא מַתִּירוֹ בְּבַת חוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that losing the שפחה כנענית makes freedom a חוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Freedom permits a בת חורין, which is a gain that balances or outweighs the loss.

steps.title: A slave prefers a loose life
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a slave prefers the loose, easy relationship with a שפחה. To him she is lowly, easy to find, and unrestricted, so losing her is a real loss in his eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: A slave is comfortable with a loose life. She is lowly to him, available to him, and unrestricted to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק by explaining why, from the slave's point of view, losing the שפחה outweighs gaining a free woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We judge the loss by what the slave himself wants. A free woman comes with marriage and its duties. A שפחה is lowly to him, always around, and has no restrictions. So for him, freedom is a loss, which supports רבי מאיר.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר holds that freeing a slave is a חוב. For a כהן's slave, he loses תרומה. For any slave, he loses the שפחה כנענית, which a slave prefers. The חכמים answer the תרומה point by saying the master could always sell him to a ישראל anyway ('מפני שהוא קנינו').

phrases.english: A slave is comfortable with a loose life:

phrases.aramaic: זִילָא לֵיהּ, שְׁכִיחָא לֵיהּ, פְּרִיצָה לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: she is lowly to him, she is available to him, she is unrestricted for him.
phrases.notes: "She" is the שפחה כנענית from step 5.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אדרבה challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Judges the loss from the slave's own point of view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being permitted to a free woman is a gain that cancels the loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: A slave prefers the loose relationship with a שפחה, so losing it is a real חוב for him.

steps.title: New משנה: Divorce and Freedom Documents Stop at Death, Money Gifts Do Not
steps.stepSummary: If someone says to give a גט to his wife or a שטר שחרור to his slave and then dies, it is not given. If he says to give a מנה to someone and then dies, it is given.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man says: 'Give this גט to my wife' or 'Give this שטר שחרור to my slave,' and then he dies. They do not give it after his death. But if he said 'Give a מנה to so-and-so' and then died, they do give it after his death.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It compares two kinds of instructions: delivering a document like a גט or a שטר שחרור, and giving money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט or a שטר שחרור must take effect while the husband or master is still alive, so once he dies the document cannot be delivered. A money gift is different: the משנה says the money is still given after he dies. The גמרא will now ask exactly how that money gift works.

keyTerms.meaning: A document that frees a slave
A sum of money, one hundred זוז (also called דינרים)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the money is given because it is an inheritance. The man gave an instruction during his life, and the question is whether that instruction still works after he died.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who says: "Give this bill of divorce to my wife,"
"this bill of freedom to my slave,"
and he died – they do not give it after death.
"Give a maneh to so-and-so,"
and he died – they give it after death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It does not depend on the earlier discussion about slaves and תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט or a שטר שחרור is not delivered after the sender's death. A money gift he ordered is given after his death.

steps.title: רב Limits the Money Case to Coins Piled in a Corner
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רב, רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא says the money is given after death only if the coins were piled up and set aside in a corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא said in the name of רב: this rule only applies when the coins were piled up and placed in a corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a limit on the משנה's money case. The money is given after death only if the coins were already set aside in a pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sounded general, but רב adds a condition. The money must be specific, set-aside coins, not just a general promise of money. This condition sets up the next question: why would piling the coins matter at all?

keyTerms.meaning: 'And this is only when...', a phrase that adds a condition

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta said
in the name of Rav:
And this is only when they are piled up
phrases.notes: 'This' means the משנה's rule that the מנה is still given after he dies.

phrases.english: and placed in a corner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limiting condition to the money part of the משנה in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The money is given after death only if the coins were piled and set aside in a corner when he gave the instruction.

steps.title: Healthy or Dying? Either Way, Why Do Piled Coins Matter?
steps.stepSummary: If the giver was healthy, piling the coins should not help, because no one did משיכה. If he was a שכיב מרע, piling should not be needed, because his words alone already work.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we talking about? If he was a healthy man, so what if the coins were piled up? Nobody pulled them! And if he was a שכיב מרע, why say 'piled' at all? Even if they were not piled it should work, because we hold that the words of a שכיב מרע count as if they were written and handed over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's condition by asking whether the giver was healthy or dying. Either way, the condition of piled coins does not seem to make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healthy person's gift of movable items needs a קנין such as משיכה, and just piling coins is not a קנין. A שכיב מרע does not need any קנין, because his words alone transfer ownership, so piling should make no difference. Both choices make רב's condition look pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
Pulling an object, a way of acquiring movable items
Count as if written down and handed over

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about whether the משנה is true. It attacks only רב's added condition about piled coins.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
If you say with a healthy person,
when they are piled, what of it?
He did not pull them!
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person getting the money. Movable items need a קנין like pulling.

phrases.english: Rather, with a person on his deathbed,
why specifically when they are piled?
Even when they are not piled, too,
since we hold
that the words of a person on his deathbed –
are as if written and handed over!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the condition of piled coins added in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's condition that the coins must be piled in a corner.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two-sided dilemma. A healthy giver needs משיכה, which piling is not. A dying giver needs nothing more than words, so piling adds nothing.

steps.title: רב זביד: A Healthy Person, and the Gift Works Through מעמד שלשתן
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד says the case is a healthy person. The gift works through רב הונא's rule that a transfer made with all three people present is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: really, it is talking about a healthy person, and it follows what רב הונא said in the name of רב. רב הונא said in the name of רב: if a man says, 'I have a מנה with you, give it to so-and-so,' and all three people are present, that person acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד answers the challenge. He picks the 'healthy person' side and shows a way the gift works without משיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a special rule called מעמד שלשתן: if the owner tells the person holding his money to give it to a third person, and all three are there, the third person acquires it even without משיכה. Piled coins that are set aside are like money held for the owner, so this rule can apply to them. That is why רב required the coins to be piled.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Really', used to keep an option the question tried to reject
In the presence of all three people (owner, holder, receiver)
'I have a מנה in your hand': money you are holding for me

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב זביד, the money in the משנה is given after the giver's death because the gift already took effect through מעמד שלשתן while he was alive and healthy. Piled coins are needed so that the money is like a deposit held for him. רב פפא explains it differently in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step introduces מעמד שלשתן, a basic way of transferring money that works without any physical act of acquiring.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
Actually, with a healthy person,
and in line with what Rav Huna said in the name of Rav –
as Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
"I have a maneh in your hand,"
"give it to so-and-so,"
in the presence of all three of them – he acquired it.
phrases.notes: The three are the owner, the one holding the money, and the one receiving it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma in step 10 by choosing the healthy-person side and giving a way the gift works without משיכה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the dilemma and supplies a קנין that works without pulling (מעמד שלשתן).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A healthy person's gift needs משיכה, so piled coins could not help.
steps.terutzMaskana: A healthy person's gift works through מעמד שלשתן. This applies to set-aside, piled coins, which are like a deposit held for the owner.

steps.title: רב פפא: The case is a dying person, and piling the coins shows which coins he meant
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says רב is talking about a שכיב מרע. The coins must be piled up because of another ruling of רב: if a dying person says 'give a מנה' without saying 'this מנה,' we worry he meant a buried מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Really, the case is a person on his deathbed. It follows another ruling of רב. רב said: A dying person said, 'Give a hundred dinars to so-and-so from my property.' If he said 'this hundred,' we give it. If he just said 'a hundred' without saying which, we do not give it. We worry that he may have meant a buried hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a second answer to the challenge from step 10. He says the giver is a dying person, and explains why the coins still need to be piled up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said that a dying person's words already work, so piling the coins should be pointless. רב פפא answers that piling does not make the gift work. It only shows which coins he meant, because if he just said 'a מנה' we worry he meant some buried money that cannot be found.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually. It brings us back to an option that was challenged before.
A person who is dying. His spoken instructions about gifts work even without a formal act of acquisition.
Like the other ruling of רב
A sum of one hundred דינרים
We are concerned, we worry about this possibility

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב פפא is saying the piling makes the gift work. For a שכיב מרע, his words alone do that. The piling only shows which specific coins he was talking about.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Really, it is about a person on his deathbed,
and it follows another ruling of Rav,
for Rav said:
A person on his deathbed who said,
'Give a hundred dinars to so-and-so from my property':
if he said 'this hundred,' we give it,
if he just said 'a hundred,' we do not give it.
We worry that perhaps
he was talking about a buried hundred.
phrases.notes: He may have meant specific hidden coins. Since we cannot find them, we cannot give other money in their place.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם בִּשְׁכִיב מְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge in step 10, different from רב זביד's answer in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case as a שכיב מרע and gives the piling a new purpose: it identifies which coins he meant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For a שכיב מרע, words alone transfer the gift, so piling the coins would be useless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words do transfer the gift, but piling makes clear he meant these coins and not a buried מנה.

steps.title: The final ruling: we do not worry about a buried מנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה does not worry that the giver meant a buried מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: we are not concerned about a buried sum.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling on רב's worry from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that a plain 'give a מנה' is not given, in case he meant buried money. The הלכה rejects that worry. So even if a dying person just says 'give a מנה,' we give it.
steps.whatToRemember: In practice, when a שכיב מרע says 'give a מנה to so-and-so,' we give it. We do not worry that he meant a buried מנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law for gifts of a dying person and goes against רב's other ruling.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is:
we are not concerned about a buried sum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on רב's worry about a buried מנה from step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה does not worry about a buried מנה, so a plain 'give a מנה' from a dying person is carried out.

steps.title: Why didn't רב פפא explain it like רב זביד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב פפא did not accept רב זביד's explanation, that the giver was healthy and the gift worked through רב הונא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason that רב פפא did not explain it like רב זביד?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks what problem רב פפא saw in רב זביד's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד said the giver was healthy and the gift worked through רב הונא's rule about a transfer made with all three people present (step 11). The גמרא wants to know what bothered רב פפא about that answer, so that he chose the dying-person explanation instead.

phrases.english: What is the reason that Rav Pappa
